newsitem.title: CHINA: Healthy body, good marriage top hopes for Chinese.
newsitem.headline: Healthy body, good marriage top hopes for Chinese.

text.p: A healthy body and a happy marriage now outweigh a high salary as the primary desires of Chinese people, a survey issued by the Guangming Daily on Friday showed.
About 64.9 percent of people said good health was their first desire in life, the newspaper said, quoting a nationwide survey of nearly 10,000 people.
In second place but trailing badly in terms of percentage was a happy marriage. About 29.9 percent of respondents said their highest hope was for a happy marriage, the survey showed.
Just 25.87 percent said they cared most about a successful career, it showed.
In a surprise development, salary was not among the top three desires of Chinese, the survey said.

Throughout the 1980s, the desire for a high salary had topped similar surveys as the market-oriented economic reforms launched by paramount leader Deng Xiaoping in 1978 offered more and new opportunities for making money.
The survey said people's desires were not influenced by income or age.
